item.title: Giants Urged to Consider Trade for RB Not Named Jonathan Taylor
item.description: As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches on November 10, the New York Giants have become one of the most active buyers on the market. Joe Schoen and company have been heavily involved in trade rumors with the deadline just days away. So far this season, the Giants have been the best team in the NFC East. Even after the season-ending injuries to quarterback Jaxson Dart and pass rusher Brian Burns, the team has continued finding ways to win football games. One of the main interests for New York in trade discussions has reportedly been upgrading the running back position. The team has been linked to multiple star running backs, including Indianapolis Colts superstar Jonathan Taylor. Saquon Barkley has been another name thrown around, as has Derrick Henry. While the flashy trade for a proven superstar would be very interesting, the Giants have other options as well. Jun 9, 2026; East Rutherford, NJ, USA; New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh answers questions from the press after the minicamp activities at Quest Diagnostics Center. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Salus-Imagn Images Giants Urged to Consider Trade for Non-Superstar Running Back Matt Levine of Giants Roundtable has suggested that Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard could be a great fit for New York. “Skattebo hasn’t been awful for the team, but his lack of ball security at times has cost the Giants. But mixing his power running with the speed and patience of Pollard could help the Giants become a well-balanced running team,” Levine wrote . “It remains unknown how the Giants will approach the trade deadline next week, but this team does want to get into the playoffs. And going after an update at running back could be one way for them to make it happen.” Pollard may not be a superstar, but he has played very good football this season. In eight games played, the 29-year-old running back has carried the football 133 times for 595 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 4.5 yards per attempt. He has also caught 14 passes for 70 yards. Making a move for Pollard would be much cheaper than a trade for Taylor, Henry, or Barkley. He would still provide a boost at the running back position, but he wouldn’t cost the Giants nearly as much draft capital. Only time will tell what New York choose to do before the deadline. However, the running back position seems to be a primary target and Pollard is a name worth monitoring. item.title: Colton Herta qualifies for F1 superlicence as Valtteri Bottas remains bullish on 2027 seat
item.description: Motorsport photo Cadillac F1 test driver Colton Herta has finally obtained the last remaining superlicence point required to drive in the series, but incumbent Valtteri Bottas remains bullish on his future with the squad. Herta conducted his sixth Friday practice session of the 2026 season at Interlagos, reaching the required threshold of 100km to earn his 40th superlicence point needed to race in F1. Read Also: F1 Brazilian GP: Lando Norris tops FP1 as Colton Herta clinches superlicence Cadillac believed the former IndyCar ace had reached that threshold last week in Mexico, but it soon emerged the Californian was still one point shy amid confusion over his previous IndyCar results. The US-owned squad rectified that error by handing Herta another Friday FP1 session in Sergio Perez's car. That allows the team to keep its options open as it considers retaining incumbent Bottas for a second year alongside Perez or handing Herta his F1 debut in 2027. The amount of time, energy and money spent by Cadillac to prepare Herta and ensure he kept churning out FP1 sessions suggests that the team is set on promoting the 26-year-old American as early as next year. But Bottas was bullish on retaining his seat for 2027 and said he was bemused by the extent of the rumours around his seat after a difficult year with the troubled Cadillac MAC-26. Alongside Herta, several other drivers have either held private talks with Cadillac or publicly applied for Bottas' seat, like Mercedes reserve driver Frederik Vesti. "I've been quite surprised about the amount of noise on that," Bottas said on Thursday. "Because I know what my situation is. And all I've heard, the team has been happy with what I'm doing. item.title: Kenny Beecham calls Warriors broadcast ‘the worst in the whole league’ after it defends Draymond Green
item.description: Credit: NBC Sports Bay Area The 2026-27 NBA season is underway, and while every NBA season brings plenty of change, it seems that some things are destined to always stay the same. The Golden State Warriors’ local NBC Sports broadcast team of Bob Fitzgerald and Kelenna Azubuike has finished in last place in Awful Announcing’s local NBA announcer rankings for three years running. Graders not only found Fitzgerald “condescending” and too focused on “teaching” the audience or complaining about referees, but the booth was also called out for its “homerism,” which even Warriors fans found excessive. That homerism reared its head again during Monday’s game between the Warriors and Phoenix Suns. Warriors forward Draymond Green was assessed a technical foul for throwing Suns center Khaman Maluach to the ground and escalating things with Suns guard Dillon Brooks afterward. However, if you let Fitzgerald and Azubuike tell it, everything Green did was within the lines. A notion so ridiculous that it wasn’t wasted on NBA content creator Kenny Beecham, who found himself on Awful Announcing’s 2026 list of rising stars in sports media. “I’m listening to this Warriors broadcast, and listen, they’ve been around for so long, this is not a new take, but I just remembered why the f*ck I don’t listen to the Warriors broadcast,” Beecham said on the Numbers On The Board podcast. Kenny speaks on the Warriors’ Broadcasters https://t.co/sWUceaucYB — Numbers On The Board (@notbpod) November 5, 2026 “It is the worst broadcast in the whole league by a wide margin, because every broadcast has to be biased. That’s why you listen to [Chicago Bulls announcer Adam Amin] and rest in peace, Stacey King. You want them to be Bulls fans, but also you don’t want them to be jack*sses while being Bulls fans. “And I feel like what they be doing in that Warriors broadcast is so jack*ssery where nobody can be wrong on the Warriors. item.title: Zach Allen and Malcom Roach Are Quietly Dominating in Denver
item.description: In a league obsessed with highlight-reel edge rushers and flashy defensive backs, the Denver Broncos have quietly built one of the NFL’s most relentless pass rushes from the inside out. Over eight weeks, the Broncos rank among the league’s top teams in sacks, and a massive share of that pressure comes from two players who almost never light up national headlines: Zach Allen and Malcolm Roach . While the spotlight stays locked on the usual suspects, these two interior defensive linemen keep collapsing pockets, generating constant chaos up the middle, and turning routine dropbacks into frantic escapes for opposing quarterbacks. Allen and Roach put up elite production, yet they remain heavily underrated. They don’t just rack up sacks and pressures. They absorb double teams, free up the edge rushers, stuff the run, and create the interior chaos that makes the Broncos defense click. Their consistency and two-way impact are a big reason Denver’s front has been so disruptive this season. Still, they fly under the national radar week after week. That needs to change. The Quiet Engine of Denver’s Front Zach Allen has spent the 2026 season doing what he does best, dominating from the interior without demanding the spotlight. Through eight weeks, the 29-year-old defensive lineman owns a 79.2 overall PFF grade (fifth among all interior defensive linemen) and leads the entire position group with 34 pressures. Those pressures have produced 4.5 official sacks, a league-high number of quarterback hits among interior players, and constant disruption that forces offenses to account for him on every snap. What makes Allen especially valuable is how he helps everyone around him. He routinely draws double teams, opening lanes for edge rushers like Nik Bonitto and creating one-on-one opportunities for Malcolm Roach. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph has publicly pushed Allen to elevate his run defense this year, and the results show: Allen’s improved strength against the run has helped solidify the entire front. Teammates notice the impact even when the national cameras don’t. As one fellow lineman put it earlier this season, Allen is “ so good at opening things up for other people.” He even made a huge special-teams play against the 49ers in Week 5, flying in to block a field-goal attempt at the end of the first half and keeping the game tied. Elite Numbers, Little Recognition The numbers only get more impressive the deeper you dig. Allen ranks first among interior defensive linemen in total pressures, sits near the top of the league in quarterback hits, and maintains an elite 82.1 PFF pass-rush grade . He has also been one of the most consistent snap-to-snap performers on the Broncos’ defense, logging a heavy workload while still producing at a high level against both the pass and the run. Few interior players in the NFL are matching this combination of volume and efficiency. Even with those numbers, the national coverage on Allen still feels surprisingly shallow.

item.title: Liverpool star named in England squad for UEFA Nations League fixtures
item.description: Liverpool star named in England squad for UEFA Nations League fixtures England Squad 2026: Rio Ngumoha Included as Thomas Tuchel Turns to Youth Thomas Tuchel has named a 25-man England squad for the final Nations League fixtures of 2026, and there are a few obvious takeaways. The first is that youth is getting its chance. The second is that a few established names are still on the outside looking in. Liverpool’s sole representative is Rio Ngumoha, the 18-year-old forward who continues to hold Tuchel’s attention. He is still at the start of his senior international career, but the pattern is clear. Tuchel saw something in Florida before the World Cup and has kept him involved since. Rio Ngumoha keeps England place Ngumoha has three senior caps so far and no goals, but that barely matters at this stage. He made his debut in the 1-0 win over New Zealand in Tampa on 6 June, coming on for the second half and becoming England’s fifth-youngest debutant. His competitive debut followed in the 2-0 Nations League win over Czechia. At 18 years and 31 days, only Wayne Rooney and Jude Bellingham were younger when making a competitive debut for England. He then added another substitute appearance against the same opposition a week later. For Liverpool, it is another sign that Ngumoha is moving quickly. He is no passenger in this squad. He is there because Tuchel wants a closer look. Photo: IMAGO Thomas Tuchel calls up fresh names Jobe Bellingham and Josh King both receive their first senior call-ups. Bellingham, now at Borussia Dortmund, steps up with his reputation growing. King, the Fulham teenager, had already trained with the squad before the 2026 World Cup and now makes the full jump. Ben White returns, while Cole Palmer is left out again and has not featured for England since March. Phil Foden is also absent. Those omissions matter because these are not fringe players. Tuchel is making choices, and they are hard ones. England Nations League schedule set England close the group stage with two demanding matches. Croatia visit Wembley on Thursday 12 November, then comes a trip to Madrid to face world champions Spain on Sunday 15 November. Finish first or second and England are into the quarter-finals next March. The forward options include Harry Kane, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers, with Eberechi Eze and Morgan Gibbs-White also selected. Former Liverpool players Trent Alexander-Arnold, now with Real Madrid, and Jarell Quansah of Bayer Leverkusen are included too. The headline, though, is simple enough. Ngumoha remains in the frame.

item.title: Man United’s Big Summer Signing Set To Miss ‘Number of Weeks’
item.description: Man United’s Big Summer Signing Set To Miss ‘Number of Weeks’ Carlos Baleba Injury Blow Leaves Manchester United Facing Midfield Test Manchester United’s season has acquired an awkward complication. Carlos Baleba, the midfielder signed for £70m in the summer to lend force and mobility to the centre of Michael Carrick’s team, now appears set for a spell on the sidelines that may stretch deep into the winter. The early indication is sobering. Baleba felt his hamstring during United’s comeback win against Roma on Tuesday, pulling up at the beginning of the second half and leaving the field in visible distress. What had first seemed likely to rule him out of the weekend now threatens to remove him from a significant portion of the schedule ahead, including the visit to Anfield on 22 November and the Champions League meeting with Sporting CP three days later. Baleba Injury Disrupts Midfield Plans For Carrick, this is damaging in ways that go beyond simple availability. Baleba has only started five matches since arriving from Brighton, in part because an ankle problem delayed the beginning of his campaign. Even so, his presence has offered a glimpse of the athletic profile United believed they were buying, a midfielder capable of covering ground quickly, recovering possession and accelerating transitions through the middle third. Now that process of integration must pause again. Carrick confirmed the prognosis remains incomplete, though the broad outline is already clear. “We don’t know, but it will be a number of weeks,” said manager Michael Carrick, “It won’t be after the international break [that Baleba returns]. It’ll be a little bit longer than that.” Photo: IMAGO Michael Carrick Weighs United Options That leaves United to navigate a busy run without a player recruited to raise the ceiling of their midfield. December alone contains seven fixtures, among them a demanding trip to Arsenal on 20 December, and there is no certainty Baleba will be restored by then. Carrick must also judge how quickly he can reintroduce Patrick Dorgu. The defender has returned to partial training after hamstring trouble of his own, though the sense from United is that caution will prevail. His involvement against Aston Villa remains undecided, with the staff wary of forcing the issue after successive muscle problems. For now, United are left with an old football truth. Carefully built plans can be altered in an instant, and the cost of absence is often measured not only in matches missed, but in momentum surrendered.

item.title: Red Sox Reportedly 'Unlikely' To Re-sign Sonny Gray; What's Plan In Rotation?
item.description: Free agent pitcher Sonny Gray Sonny Gray's mutual option was declined after a tremendous season with the Boston Red Sox. Gray has decided that he wants to keep pitching, and he should have no shortage of suitors on the open market. Despite playing in his 14th season at 36 years old, he posted a 2.72 ERA and had one of the best years of his career. He is more than just a middle rotation arm, but it does not sound like the Red Sox will bring him back. "Gray was fantastic, the team’s best starter," wrote The Boston Globe's Alex Speier. "But at this stage of the offseason, it seems unlikely the Sox will bring him back via free agency given the expected return to health of Crochet and emergence of Tolle." The Red Sox should have Crochet, Tolle, Ranger Suarez and Jake Bennett in the rotation next year. They will likely be expecting Brayan Bello to return to being a quality starter like he was in 2025, and his second-half success last season should reassure them. item.title: Tigers tweak coaching staff, bring in familiar face to front office
item.description: Detroit Tigers manager A.J. Hinch has tweaked his coaching staff, the organization has brought back a familiar face to work in the front office and the Tigers have made changes atop their medical and athletic training departments. Taken as a whole, it's clear the Tigers are trying to improve on the field for 2027 . After a rash of injuries in 2026, they are making changes to the medical side. And they have added to their baseball operations side. The Tigers named Kyle Hudson as their first base and baserunning coach on Friday, Nov. 6. Hudson, who was the Boston Red Sox third base coach, replaces Anthony Sanders. Hudson, a 39-year-old who played for Baltimore in 2011, will also help coach the outfielders. Hudson was part of Alex Cora's staff with the Red Sox and lost his job when Cora was fired in April. This move is interesting because it could provide another benefit: Maldonado will be a friendly face for Tigers pitcher Framber Valdez – Maldonado caught him in Houston. Maldonado was behind the dish when Valdez threw a no-hitter against Cleveland on Aug. 1, 2023. And Ryan Sienko, who was the Tigers catching coach, has added duties as bullpen coach. In addition, the Tigers also announced the return of Jay Sartori to the front office as vice president of baseball operations. Sartori started in 2015 under Al Avila and then worked for Scott Harris. item.title: Packers Insider Gives Team Clear Directive Before Trade Deadline
item.description: The Green Bay Packers and general manager Brian Gutekunst have been heavily involved in the NFL rumor mill leading up to the November 10 trade deadline. No one knows whether or not the team will make a big move, but the rumors have been out there that they have shown interest. Most notably, the Packers have been heavily connected to a potential blockbuster trade for Indianapolis Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor. They aren’t viewed as the front-runner to make that move, but they have at least had interest in swinging big. Over the years, Green Bay has not been known as an aggressive buyer at trade deadlines. Instead, the Packers have focused on drafting and developing, while adding veteran pieces around the edges. The trade Micah Parsons last year helped change some of that lack of aggressiveness. So far this season, the team has looked like a potential contender in some moments and a team who could miss the playoffs in others. They have the talent to be a Super Bowl caliber team. However, a move or two is needed. With that being said, one longtime Green Bay insider has spoken out with a clear directive for the team before the deadline. Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) takes off on a run Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, during the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Green Bay Packers Urged to Get Aggressive at NFL Trade Deadline Sports Illustrated’s Bill Huber believes that it’s time for the Packers to make a Super Bowl move. He thinks they should be open to making a blockbuster trade. “To do big things requires bold actions. The Packers’ championship drought is too long. Now is the time to stop ‘being in every conversation’ and actually make the move to perhaps bring another title to Titletown,” Huber wrote . That statement from Huber is music to the ears of the fans. Green Bay has typically opted to not make the final move that could lead to a Super Bowl winning run. Making the trade for Taylor could be the final missing piece. The Packers could also consider an aggressive move to fix the offensive line like trading with the Philadelphia Eagles for Landon Dickerson. Only time will tell what Green Bay chooses to do. But, it’s clear that Huber and much of the Packers’ fan base believes that the time is now for Gutekunst and the front office to take a home run swing. item.title: ‘Social media made y’all way too comfortable’: Sophie Cunningham shares a message after election
item.description: Aug 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) looks on during the second half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Sophie Cunningham had plenty to say on social media the day after the midterm elections. After sharing a post about “being better Americans” on Wednesday, the Indiana Fever guard followed it up with another message. This time, Cunningham shared a blunt quote from boxing legend Mike Tyson to her Instagram story, which took aim at people who feel comfortable disrespecting others online. Cunningham’s Post-Election Message On Wednesday, a day after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, Cunningham reposted a lengthy message from podcaster and entrepreneur Andy Frisella to her Instagram story. The post argued that the country’s problems can’t be fixed through elections alone. “One of the strangest things about our culture is how much faith we’ve placed in elections to change our lives and how little faith we’ve placed in our own ability to do the same,” the post read. “Politics is downstream of culture. We can keep changing the people in charge, passing new laws and arguing over which party has the answers … but until we change the culture fostering, producing and tolerating the problems we have as a society, nothing fundamentally changes,” it continued. The post didn’t mention a party or candidate. But the timing was notable, coming from a player who has become a lightning rod for her political views. Cunningham sparked a firestorm this summer when she said she wants to protect girls from having to compete against “biological men,” comments that critics called transphobic. Still, Cunningham has insisted that her political views fall right in the middle . “I’m very much in the middle. I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides,” Cunningham told ESPN’s Hallie Grossman in July. Mike Tyson Quote Later, Cunningham shared another message to her Instagram story, this time a quote from Tyson. “Social media made y’all way too comfortable with disrespecting people and not getting punched in the face for it,” the post read, according to OutKick . Cunningham did not add any comment of her own, and it’s unclear what, if anything, prompted her to share it. She has been vocal about how she’s treated online, though. Earlier this week, Cunningham called her critics “ psychotic ” and said they have “so much hatred in their heart.” She also recently revealed that she has hired 24/7 security . item.title: Beach volleyball pro Alex Ukkelberg comes out: 'Thankful that I'm gay'
item.description: Alex Ukkelberg said he has been living his best life as an out gay man in Los Angeles for years, having come out to family, friends and in the pro beach volleyball community. But beyond that, it wasn’t until Wednesday that he said anything about it publicly. "There's no way I could be gay," the 32-year-old from tiny Battle Lake, Minnesota said in his coming out video . "Is there?" "When you grow up in a town of less than 800 people, being different is almost always a bad thing — and it’s definitely something you want to hide," Ukkelberg wrote in the caption. "I knew I was different from a young age.. but I didn’t know what that meant." “I’ve been out for a long time to family and friends and as I shared more on social media it just felt like a good thing to say. Visibility matters,” Ukkelberg told the LGBTQ+ sports site Outsports in an interview following his social media post. See on Instagram In his video, the former women's volleyball coach for the St. Cloud State Huskies talked about the various sports he played growing up: He ran track and competed in basketball, baseball, and football. Ukkelberg said while he knew he wanted to be an athlete, he said he thought that meant "there's no way I could be gay." That's the message he said the world reinforced, as he showed a flurry of images of him as both a student-athlete and as a guy dating women. Ukkelberg confessed that he actually didn't even think of himself as gay for many years. "Up until my sophomore year of college, I genuinely thought I was straight," he said, adding that he intensely felt the weight of finally admitting his identity for the first time. “Saying the words ‘I’m gay’ out loud for the first time was really hard for me,” said Ukkelberg. He added that he struggled with his sexuality so much that for a long time, he contemplated staying in the closet. But the toll of hiding who he was while pursuing sports was too much, he said. “After quite a few years of very bad mental health, I decided I wasn’t able to give up either identity. I was just going to have to figure out how to be both, and honestly, I’m thankful that I’m gay. It’s made me a better, more empathetic person,” said Ukkelberg. "I think I’ve always found it easier to let people get to know me first before I come out to them, rather than having to break through stereotypes just to be seen for who I am," he wrote in the caption to the video. "I’ve gotten it from both directions — too gay, not gay enough.. Nobody wants to be put in a box — especially not the young gay kid from a small town in rural Minnesota." item.title: Exeter City defender James agrees new deal to 2028
item.description: Ed James first joined Exeter's academy as an eight-year-old [Shutterstock] Exeter City defender Ed James has signed a new contract to keep him at St James Park until the summer of 2028. The League Two side also has an option to extend the 21-year-old Wales Under-21 international's deal by a further 12 months. The centre-back has played 23 times in all competitions for the Grecians since making his debut in October 2022. He has become an important first team player this season, staring half of their League Two fixtures. The academy graduate has been with Exeter since he was eight and has also had loan spells at Yeovil Town and Torquay United. "Since I've come back to the club, Ed has been excellent," manager Matt Taylor told the club website. "He's a young player with huge potential. He's got great size, moves quickly for a centre-half and is aggressive. There's a lot to like about him. "He's still developing, both physically and in his understanding of the game, but he's performed well this season. He's another young player we want to build the future around. "It's another signal of our trust in the youth policy and shows the importance of the academy. "You can have all the taglines you want about developing young players, but the proof is in the pudding. You have to play them, invest in them and give them time. That's what a contract is for. "It's pleasing that some of these young players are now wanting to commit to us. item.title: James out for minimum of five games - Bompastor
item.description: James was substituted in the 6-0 win at Charlton last weekend [Getty Images] Chelsea manager Sonia Bompastor says Lauren James will be out for at least the next few weeks, casting doubt on her availability for England's World Cup qualifying play-off matches. The 25-year-old will miss at least the next five matches for the Blues, including Everton's visit to Stamford Bridge on Saturday and a crucial match against champions Manchester City next weekend. It also casts doubt on her chances of being available for England's World Cup qualifying play-off matches against Ukraine in December. After James came off in distress in the 35th minute of the 6-0 win over Charlton Athletic, Bompastor confirmed the injury: "The only one who will be missing is LJ. "She had a scan and she has an injury in her hamstring, so we won't see her until the end of this block." There was more positive news for Chelsea, with midfielder Lexi Potter, who made her England debut last month, back after missing the trip to Charlton. Chelsea, meanwhile, are top of the WSL table having won matches both with and without James this season. Bompastor added: "Of course we know how good Lauren is for us and for the team. "Also, my job is to make sure I find solutions when some players are not available and not playing for the team. I think the good thing is that when I looked at some of the statistics from last week, we are a team who are able to score through different players. "The last game we had against Charlton, a lot of players were involved in scoring again. Also, I think every player on the pitch had a shot on goal. "Even if it was not always a great one, at least all of the players who were on the pitch had a shot on goal. I think that's a good thing and, again, my job now is to make sure I find the solutions without LJ on the pitch." Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

item.description: Panthers sign ex-Eagles, Raiders cornerback before Week 9 game vs. Broncos originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Carolina Panthers are sitting atop the NFC South heading into Week 9, but there is some real concern about this team with a 3-4 record following two brutal losses. They lost 43-13 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and then 27-19 to the Green Bay Packers . While their run defense struggled against the Buccaneers, their pass defense couldn't stop the Packers in Week 8. To try to fix things on the back end of the defense, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Panthers are signing 26-year-old cornerback Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad. Panthers sign Jakorian Bennett to bolster CB depth "The Panthers signed former Raiders and Eagles CB Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad," Rapoport reported. This isn't a massive move for the Panthers, but considering the team's shaky defensive back depth, Bennett might get real playing time in the not-too-distant future. Will Lee III, Mike Jackson, Akayleb Evans, and Jaycee Horn are all hurt right now. Only Lee has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Broncos . If Lee can't go, the Panthers will be down to relying on Malcolm DeWalt IV a lot, as the rest of their CB depth chart is banged up. Bennett might see a role right away as the Panthers' CB room is dealing with a lot of injury issues. He has 12 passes defended with 65 total tackles in his career to go with a solid 81.5 passer rating allowed. Across the 2025 and 2024 seasons, he's allowed a 66.5 and 67.7 passer rating, respectively. He hasn't played in 2026 as he's dealt with an injury issue, but now with the Panthers, he might be good to go. item.title: Bo Naylor Reveals He Didn't Know Depths of MLB Gambling
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers catcher Bo Naylor If any MLB players didn't believe that allegedly fixing games came with serious consequences, the images from the federal trial involving Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz this week should have changed their minds. Clase and Ortiz were in New York on Thursday to face conspiracy charges for allegedly fixing individual pitches for prop bets during the 2025 season. Catcher Bo Naylor, who was a teammate of both pitchers with the Cleveland Guardians at the time, testified that he "didn't know" individual pitches could even be bet on. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "I didn't know that before," Naylor said, according to The Associated Press. "I didn't know that until (this) situation." Prosecutors expressed disbelief that Naylor could be unaware of the nature of such bets, according to the AP report, and showed video of multiple pitches that have been called into question. Naylor was called upon to testify because, as a catcher, he would have been involved in game-planning and calling pitches for Clase and Ortiz, and might have known if they didn't throw the pitches he'd called. When pitches missed the strike zone -- in some cases, spiked into the dirt or airmailed to the backstop -- Naylor testified that he simply chalked it up to even the best pitchers often missing their spots. Naylor appeared in 207 games as a catcher over the 2024-2025 seasons with Cleveland. He was limited to 27 total games with the Guardians this season before he was traded to the Milwaukee Brewers, with whom he played only three games. item.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Lando Norris tops FP1 as Colton Herta clinches superlicence
item.description: Motorsport photo Lando Norris was fastest in Free Practice 1 at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix, leading Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. Norris outpaced Antonelli by 0.082s on the soft rubber with a time of 1m11.717s, while Verstappen and Hamilton were two and three tenths adrift respectively, with the top-four teams again all close together. Not all of them were happy, however, with Verstappen complaining over team radio about a long-time problem of the RB22: “Unacceptable, man. Unacceptable, these downshifts. What the ****?” Later on, he mentioned yet another issue: “There’s something wrong with my steering. It’s getting harder and harder to turn the wheel.” There were hefty lock-ups galore in Turn 1 for veterans and rookies alike – and there were many of the latter in action. The most prominent of them undoubtedly was Rafael Camara, with Haas’ 2027 driver making an early F1 debut at home this weekend following Esteban Ocon’s fallout with the team. Formula 2’s championship leader was 18th-fastest in this session, nearly nine tenths slower than team-mate Oliver Bearman. One rookie who did outpace the sister car was Alpine’s Gabriele Mini, who took seventh place with a 1m12.569s, 0.085s quicker than Franco Colapinto. No other rookie run driver made it into the top 10; McLaren’s Leonardo Fornaroli was 11th (+1.116s vs Norris), Williams’ Luke Browning 17th (+0.080s vs Alex Albon, who had a mechanical problem) and Cadillac’s Colton Herta 20th (+0.904s vs Valtteri Bottas). Gabriele Mini, Alpine F1 Gabriele Mini, Alpine F1 Herta’s trouble-free session – other than a mammoth lock-up into Turn 1 – should theoretically mean he will collect the final required point for an FIA superlicence, making him eligible to a 2027 F1 seat should Cadillac elect to promote him next year. Ferrari’s Dino Beganovic and Audi’s Freddie Slater propped up the classification after encountering technical issue which prevented them from setting soft-tyre times and restricted their mileage. “The car has just switched off,” Slater said, causing a red flag just 12 minutes into the session. The pair completed 11 and seven laps respectively. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.description: Official: Paul Nebel extends contract with Mainz 05 As officially announced by the Bundesliga club this afternoon, Paul Nebel has extended his contract with 1. FSV Mainz 05. The midfielder, who joined the club at Bruchweg as a 13-year-old, progressed through all the youth teams at Mainz's academy. Nebel has worn the 05ers' jersey for over ten years, with the exception of a two-year loan spell at second division side Karlsruher SC. Still only 24 years of age, Nebel has already made 95 appearances in all competitions for Mainz, providing 15 goals and 18 assists. “Paul is the prime example of how a player from our own youth academy can develop into a very important player for our Bundesliga team. “He has shown a lot of passion, patience and a down-to-earth attitude,” explained Mainz sporting director Niko Bungert. "Paul is an important and reliable pillar for our team and someone who has shown in recent years that he is always there when needed. "We are happy that we have found a very good solution for our future together with him.”

item.description: Tigers could pursue another Yankees All-Star 2B after Gleyber Torres originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Tigers could be looking for a new second baseman during this offseason. Gleyber Torres is a free agent after spending the past two seasons with the Tigers, hitting .260/.364/.363 with eight home runs and a 105 OPS+ in 96 games in 2026. Torres has become a great on-base guy the last few years, but he offers little to no value with his legs on the basepaths. Detroit could have Zach McKinstry and Hao-Yu Lee split time at second base, or they could target another former New York Yankees middle infielder. "The lineup is less of a concern, but Jazz Chisholm Jr. to Detroit wouldn't be a colossal surprise. "At any rate, the last time the Yankees let a multiple-time All-Star second baseman walk in free agency without even extending him a qualifying offer, Gleyber Torres ended up with the Tigers. Perhaps they bring in Chisholm to replace him," Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller wrote. Chisholm doesn't get on base nearly enough to match Torres' .364 OBP, but he hit 19 homers and stole a career-high 41 bases this past season. The Tigers stole 58 bases across 162 games, just 17 more than Chisholm swiped by himself. Obviously, Chisholm's been a topic of discussion for some negative reasons, including playing the field with a lollipop in his mouth. You'd like to think the Tigers would make it clear that those kinds of things are not allowed, especially under manager A.J. Hinch. They could use a few additions to the starting rotation too, but signing Chisholm would be a solid start to the offseason for Detroit. item.title: Arizona’s Tommy Lloyd takes laundry list of learning lessons from first win of season vs. Cal Poly
item.description: Eakin Howard-Imagn Images Arizona’s Tommy Lloyd takes laundry list of learning lessons from first win of season vs. Cal Poly appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After falling to UCLA in the season opener, Tommy Lloyd and the No. 5 Arizona Wildcats got their first win of the season with a 104-84 beatdown of Cal Poly at home. Motiejus Krivas, who returned to Arizona amid NBA buzz , led the Wildcats with 30 points and eight rebounds. During his post-game interview with Andy Katz, Lloyd shared what he was most satisfied with in win No. 1. “Getting the win’s nice. We’re obviously a team that’s figuring itself out. Cal Poly, give them a ton of credit. They played so hard and just kept coming. We had some really good moments. Hopefully we could build on it. We had some moments when we kind of let up a little bit. You can’t let up at this level. Our team has to establish the effort we need to play with all the time. So it’s a little bit of a work in progress,” Lloyd said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) And when asked what he wanted to build on, the reigning Naismith Coach of the Year winner got on his team for failing to rebound and being “allergic” to loose balls. While Lloyd wasn’t pleased with the team’s rebounding, the Wildcats still had a 44-30 edge on the boards. The Euro frontcourt of Krivas and Ivan Kharchenkov led the way with 18 rebounds combined, while backup big man Evan Otten added seven boards in just nine minutes. One area that Arizona will need to get better at is 3-point shooting. They went just 4-of-14 from beyond the arc after going a mere 7-of-30 in the loss against UCLA. Lloyd and the Wildcats will look to improve on that and their ability to get to loose balls in their next game against Northern Arizona on Tuesday. item.title: Bijan Robinson Chases Acting Dreams Beyond The Field
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images While the Atlanta Falcons are fighting for their season, the 24-year-old running back is actively planning his life after the gridiron. He told the New York Post that he is taking serious steps to launch an acting career. He even wants to star in a romantic comedy. This is more than a hobby for a rich athlete. He is enrolling in acting classes to learn the craft from the ground up. He appeared as himself on the Disney Channel show “Bunk’d: Learning The Ropes” last July. He also made a cameo in the Netflix series “Outerbanks” in October. Those roles were fun, but he wants more. He said he is ready to move past commercials and into serious drama. “I’m willing to kind of explore anything more on the drama side,” Robinson said on behalf of Invisalign. A Plan for Life After Football The 2026 season has been tough for the Falcons. They sit at 3-5 after a 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Robinson knows the team needs him to be better. He has 780 rushing yards and four touchdowns so far. Yet he refuses to accept praise as the league’s top back. “I’ll be honest, like, I don’t feel like I’m playing like that right now,” Robinson said, in comments shared by Falcons reporter Daniel Flick. He demands more from himself for the offense to succeed. He launched his own DJ series called “Spin Zone” in September 2024. He sees these projects as a way to grow as a person. “I want to continue to put myself in different brackets of life,” Robinson said. He plans to dig deep into acting classes at the end of the year. He wants to gain the talent and charisma needed to succeed on screen, not just because he is an NFL star. Advice for Struggling Stars Robinson uses his own experiences to help others facing pressure. He is in Madrid this week to play the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 8. He plans to meet with Real Madrid soccer stars Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé before the game. Vinícius is going through a slump and dealing with a four-game suspension. Robinson offered simple advice to help the Brazilian player. “I’ll tell (Vinícius), just stay the course. Don’t worry about external noise,” Robinson said. He warned that listening to critics can hurt a player’s mind. He knows what it feels like to have bad weeks. He told Vinícius to trust that God’s plan for his career would be amazing. “If you have an up-and-down or a low or something like that, we all have those moments and we all had those weeks,” Robinson said. The running back wears number 7, just like Vinícius. They met through a jeweler a few years ago.

item.title: Oscar Piastri pays tribute to Australian F1 legend Alan Jones following his death
item.description: Motorsport photo McLaren's Oscar Piastri has paid tribute to Alan Jones following the death of Australia's 1980 Formula 1 world champion. Jones died at the age of 80 on 5 November 2026, following a short illness. He won 12 grands prix, celebrated 24 podium finishes and gave Williams its first drivers' title. He also remains the last Australian to have won the Australian Grand Prix at Calder Park in 1980. Jones competed in the championship from 1975 to 1981, in 1983 and again from 1985 to 1986. In addition to Williams, he also drove for Hesketh, Hill, Surtees, Shadow, Arrows and Haas-Lola. Speaking to F1.com at Interlagos ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix weekend, Piastri said: "It's obviously a very sad day. A life that should be very well celebrated. I think [he was] a guy who obviously had a lot of success on the racetrack and was Australia’s most recent world champion. "But I think also the person he was, you know, a very straightforward person, straight to the point. On a personal level as well, he often had nice things to say about me, which was nice." Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones The Australian driver revealed he had driven the Williams in which Jones won his title. "I’ve had the honour to drive his world championship-winning car as well, so [it was] very cool to be able to experience that and connect with him in some kind of way. A sad day, but a day that should celebrate a great life. "Obviously, he was a long, long time before me, and I never had much interaction with Alan. But I think in a lot of ways, he kind of embodied the Australian spirit – very tough, saying it how it is, saying what he thinks, and I think that’s probably the biggest thing. "Anyone who’s won a world championship in F1 has clearly achieved it through talent, hard work, all kinds of other things, so I think that probably says enough."
